profile: Derschaun Monique Brown, Executive Director, Friends of the Children-Detroit (Detroit, MI). Speaks on long-term salaried professional mentoring (ages 4-6 through graduation), Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs), ending generational poverty, the two-generation (2Gen) family approach, foster-care-involved youth, Detroit youth, and Black women in nonprofit leadership. DPS graduate, former teacher, 25+ years mentoring. Michigan and Midwest first; national and virtual stages when the audience fits.

opportunities.name: ILA Women and Leadership Conference (8th)
opportunities.geography: St. Catherine University, St. Paul, MN
opportunities.format: Session proposal via Sessionize (formats not listed)
opportunities.deadlineNote: Call for speakers closes Nov 13, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.
opportunities.why: Theme tracks include mobilizing grassroots communities and bridging generational divides, which fits her story of a DPS graduate now leading a 12+ year mentoring model in Detroit.
opportunities.watchouts: Global, academic-leaning audience. Pitch the leadership story, not program operations. Travel at her own cost unless stated otherwise.
opportunities.nextStep: Submit by Nov 13: one session on leading a Black-woman-led chapter of a national nonprofit and building trust with families over 12+ years.

opportunities.name: NASW 2027 National Conference
opportunities.compensation: Not stated; NASW presenters typically register at their own cost
opportunities.why: National social-work stage. FOTC enrolls children with 2+ ACEs and pairs them with salaried professional mentors, a workforce model social workers rarely see.
opportunities.watchouts: Very competitive and clinically oriented. Frame it around ACEs-informed practice and outcomes, not fundraising.
opportunities.nextStep: Submit by Nov 16: 'Paid professional mentors as an ACEs intervention: 12-year relationships and two-generation family work.'

opportunities.name: ZERO TO THREE LEARN Conference 2027
opportunities.format: Lecture (60 min), Synergy Circle (60 min), Baby Talk (15 min), Issue Intensive (120 min), digital poster
opportunities.compensation: Presenters pay a discounted registration (was $285 in 2025)
opportunities.deadlineNote: Proposals due Dec 11, 2026, 11:59 PM PST. Notifications by mid-April 2027.
opportunities.why: Biggest national early-childhood stage. FOTC enrolls at ages 4-6 and works with caregivers (2Gen), which matches the prenatal-to-5 focus.
opportunities.watchouts: Event is a year out, but the deadline is inside the window. The audience is birth to 5, so lead with the early-enrollment and caregiver side.
opportunities.nextStep: Draft a 60-minute Lecture or Synergy Circle on enrolling 4-6 year olds with ACEs and supporting their caregivers. Submit by Dec 11.

opportunities.name: NASW-Michigan Statewide Conference 2027
opportunities.geography: Sheraton Grand Rapids Airport Hotel, Grand Rapids, MI
opportunities.format: Breakouts and keynotes (2 keynotes + 2 breakout blocks per day)
opportunities.deadlineNote: Event page says RFPs for presenters are being accepted. Deadline not confirmed; the page could not be fully loaded.
opportunities.why: Michigan's main social-work conference (theme: 'Woven Together'). Her ACEs-informed mentoring model and Detroit outcomes speak directly to Michigan practitioners.
opportunities.watchouts: Deadline unknown and could be close. Confirm this week.
opportunities.nextStep: Email jfreeman.naswmi@socialworkers.org to ask for the RFP link and deadline, then submit a breakout (or pitch a keynote).

opportunities.name: Michigan AEYC Annual Early Childhood Conference 2027
opportunities.organizer: Michigan Association for the Education of Young Children
opportunities.geography: Amway Grand Plaza, Grand Rapids, MI
opportunities.deadlineNote: A session proposal form is posted on the RFP page. Deadline for the 2027 annual conference not confirmed.
opportunities.why: Largest early-childhood gathering in Michigan (~3,000 attendees). Her children are enrolled at ages 4-8 and she is a former teacher.
opportunities.watchouts: The audience is classroom educators and directors, so give them practical takeaways: spotting ACEs and partnering with mentors and families.
opportunities.nextStep: Open the Michigan AEYC RFP page, confirm the annual-conference deadline, and submit a family-engagement session.

opportunities.name: Michigan Federation for Children and Families: Senior Management Conference 2027
opportunities.organizer: Michigan Federation for Children and Families
opportunities.geography: Crystal Mountain Resort, Thompsonville, MI (2025 and 2026 venue)
opportunities.format: Workshop / general session; keynote call in 2025
opportunities.deadlineNote: 2027 call not posted yet. Past deadlines were Feb 24, 2025 and Feb 20, 2026, so expect a late-February 2027 deadline.
opportunities.why: About 200 CEOs and senior leaders of Michigan child and family agencies. The 2025 call listed 2Gen approaches and trauma-informed leadership as topics.
opportunities.watchouts: Advanced leadership audience. Bring leadership tools, not a program overview.
opportunities.nextStep: Watch michfed.org from January. Prepare a keynote pitch and a leadership workshop so both are ready when the call opens.

opportunities.name: Michigan Community Action Summer Conference 2027
opportunities.organizer: Michigan Community Action (state association of 27 Community Action Agencies)
opportunities.compensation: The proposal form asks speakers to choose no fee, an honorarium, or a fee
opportunities.deadlineNote: 2026 proposals were due Apr 3, 2026. Expect the 2027 RFP around February-March with an early-April deadline.
opportunities.why: An anti-poverty audience statewide. Ending generational poverty is FOTC-Detroit's stated mission, and 2Gen fits Community Action's whole-family model.
opportunities.watchouts: Sessions must be interactive; lecture-only proposals are discouraged.
opportunities.nextStep: Watch for the 2027 RFP in February. Propose a keynote and request an honorarium.

opportunities.name: National Mentoring Summit (2028 workshop call)
opportunities.deadlineNote: 2027 call ran Apr 13 - May 31, 2026 (closed). Expect the 2028 call in mid-April 2027 with a late-May deadline.
opportunities.why: The top national stage for her field (~1,000 attendees). A paid, 12-year professional mentor model stands out in a mostly volunteer-mentor field.
opportunities.watchouts: No selling or fundraising from the stage. Workshops must give practical tools.
opportunities.nextStep: Consider attending Jan 28-29, 2027 to network. Draft the workshop by April, ideally co-presenting with another Friends of the Children chapter or a Friend (mentor).

opportunities.name: Michigan Community Schools & Family Engagement Conference 2027
opportunities.organizer: Michigan Community Schools Coalition + MiLEAP Office of Family Partnerships
opportunities.deadlineNote: 2026 proposals were due May 22, 2026. Expect the 2027 call around April-May.
opportunities.why: A statewide family-school-community partnership audience. FOTC-Detroit enrolls through school referrals and runs a 2Gen caregiver approach.
opportunities.watchouts: State-run call. Announcements go out through MiLEAP and ISD lists, so it is easy to miss.
opportunities.nextStep: Ask a referring school partner to forward the 2027 call when it posts. Prep a school-referral partnership story.

opportunities.name: YDRC Spring Summit (Detroit)
opportunities.geography: Detroit, MI (YDRC convenes at Durfee Innovation Society, 2470 Collingwood, which is also FOTC-Detroit's address)
opportunities.deadlineNote: YDRC says to stay tuned for the next Spring Summit. No speaker call posted.
opportunities.why: Easy win: Southeast Michigan youth-development professionals, run from the same building as FOTC-Detroit. A good first stage for building a speaker reel.
opportunities.watchouts: Organizers may invite speakers directly rather than run an open call. Ask now.
opportunities.nextStep: Email or walk over to YDRC this month and offer a workshop or panel slot on long-term mentoring for the Spring Summit.

opportunities.name: NAEYC Annual Conference 2027
opportunities.organizer: National Association for the Education of Young Children
opportunities.format: 1.25 or 1.5 hr sessions, 3 hr sessions, posters
opportunities.compensation: Presenters register at a discounted rate
opportunities.deadlineNote: 2027 call not posted yet. The 2017 conference's deadline was mid-January, so the window may open soon. Confirm.

opportunities.watchouts: Limit of two proposals per person. Membership may matter. Confirm when the call opens.
opportunities.nextStep: Check naeyc.org/annual/present in December and submit as soon as the 2027 call opens.

opportunities.name: TEDxDetroit 2027 speaker application
opportunities.format: Curated TEDx talk (selected from 300+ applications in past years)
opportunities.deadlineNote: Past speaker applications opened spring or summer, with deadlines from June to September. The 2027 cycle has not been announced.
opportunities.why: High-visibility, recorded talk. Her story as a DPS graduate now leading a generational-poverty solution fits TEDxDetroit's focus on Detroit storytelling.
opportunities.watchouts: Very competitive. Needs one sharp idea, not an org overview. A video sample helps.
opportunities.nextStep: Draft a one-idea talk concept by spring. Apply as soon as the 2027 application opens.

opportunities.name: Parenting Awareness Michigan (PAM) Conference
opportunities.geography: Lansing, MI (2026: James B. Henry Center)
opportunities.deadlineNote: The 2026 call has passed. The 2027 call date is unknown.
opportunities.why: Its 2026 call asked for trauma and ACEs, protective factors, resilience, and engaging male caregivers, which matches her 2Gen and ACEs work.
opportunities.watchouts: Strength-based framing is required. No promotional sessions.
opportunities.nextStep: Watch for the 2027 call in spring/summer and adapt the ACEs and caregiver workshop for it.

opportunities.name: Michigan CASA Annual Conference 2027

opportunities.why: A paid workshop for child-welfare advocates. FOTC-Detroit serves foster-care-involved children, and the 2026 topics included trauma and poverty.
opportunities.watchouts: Outside the 6-month window. Keep it on the list for the spring scan.
opportunities.nextStep: Re-check in April 2027 for the 2027 RFP.

opportunities.name: NBCDI National Conference
opportunities.deadlineNote: No 2026 or 2027 conference or call found on nbcdi.org as of Nov 5, 2026.
opportunities.why: A national stage centered on Black children and families, aligned with her Detroit work and healing-centered framing.
opportunities.watchouts: The conference schedule is unclear. Do not plan around it until NBCDI posts dates.
opportunities.nextStep: Sign up for NBCDI updates. The weekly scan will flag a call when one posts.
